'''Tarhana''' is a dried food ingredient, based on a [[Fermentation (food)|fermented]] mixture of grain and [[yogurt]] or [[fermented milk]], found in [[Central Asian cuisine|Central Asian]], [[Balkan cuisine|Southeast European]], and [[Middle Eastern cuisine|Middle Eastern]] cuisines. Dry tarhana has a texture of coarse, uneven crumbs, and it is usually made into a thick [[soup]] with water, stock, or milk. As it is both acidic and low in moisture, the milk proteins keep for long periods. Tarhana is very similar to some kinds of [[kashk]].

Regional variations of the name include [[Armenian language|Armenian]] {{Lang|hy|թարխանա}} ({{lang|hy-Latn|tarkhana}}); [[Greek language|Greek]] {{Lang|el|τραχανάς}} ({{lang|el-Latn|trahanás}}) or {{Lang|el|ξυνόχονδρος}} ({{lang|el-Latn|xynohondros}}); [[Persian language|Persian]] {{Lang|fa|ترخینه، ترخانه، ترخوانه}} ({{lang|fa-Latn|tarkhineh, tarkhāneh, tarkhwāneh}}); [[Kurdish language|Kurdish]] {{lang|ku-Latn|tarxane}}; [[Albanian language|Albanian]] {{Lang|sq|trahana}} or {{lang|sq|tërhana}}; [[Bulgarian language|Bulgarian]] {{Lang|bg|трахана}} or {{Lang|bg|тархана}} ({{lang|bg-Latn|trahana, tarhana}}); [[Serbo-Croatian]] {{lang|sh-Latn|tarana}}, {{lang|sh-Latn|tarhana}} or {{lang|sh-Latn|trahana}}; [[Hungarian language|Hungarian]] {{Lang|hu|[[tarhonya]]}}; [[Turkish language|Turkish]] {{Lang|tr|tarhana}}.

The [[Armenian cuisine|Armenian]] {{lang|hy-Latn|tarkhana}} is made up of [[matzoon]] and eggs mixed with equal amounts of wheat flour and starch. Small pieces of dough are prepared and dried and then kept in glass containers and used mostly in soups, dissolving in hot liquids.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tarkhana|url=http://dic.academic.ru/dic.nsf/enc_pohlebkin/2166/%D0%A2%D0%90%D0%A0%D0%A5%D0%90%D0%9D%D0%90|publisher=Great Encyclopedia of Culinary Arts|access-date=6 March 2015|language=ru}}</ref> The [[Greek cuisine|Greek]] {{lang|el-Latn|trahanas}} contains only [[cracked wheat]] or a ''[[couscous]]''-like paste and [[fermented milk]]. The [[Turkish cuisine|Turkish]] {{lang|tr|tarhana}} consists of cracked wheat (or flour), yoghurt, and vegetables, fermented and then dried. In [[Cyprus]], it is considered a national specialty, and is often served with pieces of [[halloumi]] cheese in it. In [[Albanian cuisine|Albania]] it is prepared with wheat, yoghurt and butter, and served with hot [[olive oil]] and [[feta]] cheese.
